AW-S planning note: the detached studio at 14 Alder Walk has a flat roof and its own proposed inverter position by the pottery sink. The roof sketch shows a low vent that constrains the first layout.

Studio flat-roof survey: the low vent is farther from the rear parapet than the draft drawing showed. The installer will revise panel spacing for AW-S. The proposed inverter position remains beside the pottery sink pending their assessment.

LL-22 planning at 22 Linden Lane: the west-facing roof is partly shaded by a neighbor's tall pear tree. We asked for a shade review before choosing between the two array sizes on the household's preliminary quote.

Our neighborhood quote clinic will compare QC-8's chimney-shadow review with LL-22's pear-tree shade review. Bring the timed Quarry Close roof image and Linden Lane tree image so the installer can explain each household's outstanding layout question.

Eastmere display planning joins MC-71, the 1892 wall chart, and MC-72, the 1910 pocket map. Photograph the same North Pier area on both for the exhibition comparison, while retaining each object's own treatment record and accession label.
MC-72 intake: Eastmere harbor pocket map, dated 1910, folded into a blue cloth case. The central fold has cracked through two harbor labels. Unlike the wall format, this object has no hanging rod.

Pocket Eastmere map update: the blue case is stable enough for photography. The brittle central fold still needs support during opening. Put the unfolded view and the closed-case view together in MC-72's condition record.
